The docstring states this too: "If the user aborts the input by sending an interrupt signal this function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception."

Bug #1 fixed. In `src/click/core.py` (`Option.__init__`), a flag with a missing default was always forced to `default=False`, even when `required=True`, so `value_is_missing(False)` was False and `MissingParameter` was never raised. Changed to only apply the implicit flag default when the option is not required. Now `--foo` (is_flag=True, required=True) invoked with no args exits 2 with "Error: Missing option '--foo'.", while non-required flags still default to False. Full pre-existing suite: 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Bug #11 fixed. In `src/click/decorators.py`, `argument` popped `cls` out of the shared `attrs` dict inside the returned decorator, so reusing the same decorator object lost the custom class after the first use. It now takes `cls` as an explicit keyword argument (defaulting to `Argument`) and never mutates `attrs`. Verified: same decorator reused on two commands keeps the custom class; full suite still 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Bug #15 fixed. In `src/click/types.py`, `Path.convert` resolved symlinks by `os.readlink` + `os.path.realpath`, so a *relative* symlink target was resolved against the current working directory instead of the symlink's own directory. It now uses `os.fsdecode(pathlib.Path(rv).resolve())`, which resolves relative and absolute symlinks correctly on all platforms. Verified with relative/absolute symlinks from a different cwd; full suite still 488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed.
